text: In the problem of universals, realism and nominalism differ in that:
choices: realism denies abstract objects, while nominalism affirms them
realism holds there is a single property (a universal) shared by all red things, whereas nominalism admits only particulars
both deny that properties exist in any sense
nominalism posits Platonic Forms, while realism posits tropes
explanation: Realism about universals affirms one entity — redness — wholly present in each red thing (Plato's Forms, Armstrong), while nominalism admits only particulars, treating 'redness' as a class, a resemblance structure, or a bundle of tropes. Option D swaps the labels (Forms are realist, tropes nominalist), and A and C misstate both views.
